reviews.text: Unspeakable. Emergency Sunday night, no doctors for dogs or cats, only a nurse on call.

Very kind at the reception, friendly and prepared vets, also very patient with our Coco, I think they will remember him for a long time, thank you for taking care of him and having looked after him so that he can return to jumping happily at home.....

The facility and organization are fine in my opinion (based on my experience). A slightly negative note is for the reception staff who take and record calls. I've noticed that they often make mistakes when transcribing information, which then ends up on your pet's file. Also, a small but significant issue: the scales used to weigh small animals aren't very accurate. It costs a few euros to buy a new one that works. Otherwise, nothing to complain about.

My second experience was much more positive than the first. The staff were very thorough, both in terms of competence, hospitality, and helpfulness. I thank and recommend this clinic.
We were treated by Dr. Walter Scarabello, a truly delightful, knowledgeable, and helpful person. The back office staff were extremely kind and efficient.
We brought a stray kitten. The doctor who welcomed us and examined her was truly fantastic, very kind and empathetic. Thank you so much!

Quite disappointing experience.
We brought in a wild baby rabbit that sadly had been injured by one of our dachshunds. She had two broken legs, so we immediately took her to the clinic, arriving before 20:00.
We were told that simply examining the rabbit would cost €85. We accepted, even though this was a wild animal and not our pet, so a second thought would have been nice before charging the full admission price. But ok, it is our dog who did it so… ok. After the examination, we were told that the only option was euthanasia, costing another €30. Again, we accepted without hesitation because we didn’t want her to suffer.
What was really upsetting was the final bill. Because the consultation and paperwork took some time and it was now after 20:00, an additional night-shift charge was added, bringing the total to €160. We had arrived before 20:00, yet we were still charged as if we had arrived during the night shift. In the end, we paid €150 only because of a €10 discount from the pet-store card — not because the clinic chose to show any compassion or consideration.
We were not expecting free treatment. We were willing to pay to make sure this poor animal didn’t suffer. But the whole experience left us feeling that the priority was the bill rather than the welfare of a helpless wild animal.
Very sad and disappointing experience. A little compassion in a situation like this would have meant a lot.
Excellent exotic vets, competent and professional, two of our hamsters were patients

We visited the clinic several times in August and September for our rabbit, both as an emergency and as part of a diagnostic and therapeutic program. We were treated, even at night, with extreme kindness, efficiency, and professionalism. The rabbit underwent diagnostic tests (blood tests, ultrasound, and cranial CT scan) promptly, and the results were always communicated clearly, promptly, comprehensively, and satisfactorily. Even during the days of hospitalization following surgery, we were promptly informed and reassured. We are very satisfied and grateful.
5 stars because Dr. Mani was very kind, competent, and gentle with my 13-year-old poodle.

My first experience at MyPetClinic, where I took my lop-eared rabbit, and I was truly satisfied. The facility is modern and very well organized, and the wait time was reasonable. The reception staff were very friendly and helpful. Dr. Picozzi was very clear, thorough, and attentive in providing all the explanations. I felt well looked after and in good hands. Recommended!

I brought my dead dog home at 4:00 AM. They didn't even open the door, telling me to come back later because they were busy with surgery. What do you think I was supposed to do with the dead dog? Some people should change their careers! Disgusting!
It's a shame they can't give zero stars.
Welcoming environment with efficient and friendly staff. Our trusted vet for five years. Our exotic animal vet was truly perfect! Highly recommended.
Dr. Elena Sgamma is incredibly kind and professional. She explained everything to me with the sensitivity and candor needed in confusing situations. Thank you very much.
I take care of all my furry pets and in the past I also had Gallina taken care of by them, who treated me with great love and professionalism.

A 10-month-old rat was brought to the emergency room on Tuesday night for severe neurological symptoms that appeared out of nowhere. After an examination, they sent me home with treatments that didn't seem to work. In less than 48 hours, I returned, explaining that there had been a slight improvement and then a relapse. The rat wasn't eating.

They suggested keeping her hospitalized until the following Tuesday for a CT scan and, if necessary, starting the appropriate and necessary treatment for the probable pituitary tumor. I was reassured several times that once the test was done, they would raise the dosages to therapeutic levels. I go to see her almost every day with her little sisters, and every day they tell me how she continues to get worse. I assume the doctors are careless with the animals, as she had very strong urine odors and markings from other animals, such as dogs and cats. To make matters worse, at each visit, I was greeted by a completely different doctor who seemed completely unaware of the situation.

The CT scan was scheduled for Tuesday afternoon. They called me Tuesday morning to tell me she didn't make it.

As if that weren't enough, they're trying to capitalize on her death by insisting on a now-useless biopsy because "it would help science understand what happened."

What happened is that you held a little creature hostage for almost a week, delaying the care she needed until she was no longer able to make it. Any doctor worth their salt would have invited me to another clinic where they could have performed the CT scan much more quickly given the urgency. They preferred to wait until the last minute, at the expense of the little girl who still had her whole life ahead of her. I consulted my usual vet, who confirmed that in cases like this, it's crucial to act urgently and within hours, not days. She had to wait a week, and with each visit I found her more disheveled, dirty, smelly, and in disrepair. A traumatic experience. and neither this review, nor the wasted money, nor the tears shed, nor the days spent in bed will ever be enough to bring her back.
